item.title: Wildfires and Colorado’s Luxury Real Estate Market: Lessons from Marshall, Waldo, High Park, and Black Forest
item.dc:creator: Christine Gwinnup
item.description: What Marshall, Waldo Canyon, High Park and Black Forest teach Colorado luxury buyers and sellers about wildfire insurance, pricing and recovery.
item.content:encoded:
Colorado’s high-end neighborhoods are resilient, but the recovery arc after a wildfire is not uniform. The variables that reset value are insurance adequacy, lending mechanics, and rebuild velocity—influenced by location and buyer demographics. This analysis distills what affluent sellers and discerning buyers need to know.

item.title: The Psychology Of Pricing: Why $2,495,000 Beats $2,500,000 In Luxury Real Estate
item.dc:creator: Christine Gwinnup
item.description: How anchoring bias, odd-number pricing and search-bracket strategy actually play out when pricing an estate home in Northern Colorado's luxury market.
item.content:encoded:
Setting a listing price for a luxury home is no simple task. Your agent will research comparable estate-level properties in your area to determine market value, but that's only the first step. Next, you have to set the specific number — and at the top of the market, that number does real psychological work.

Buyer psychology is a huge consideration when marketing a high-end property. Purchasing a multimillion-dollar home is an emotional experience as much as a financial one, and a buyer's gut reaction to a listing can shape the entire negotiation. At this price tier, a $5,000 adjustment can change which search results a home even appears in.
